summary: David Morgan works in religious studies and history and archaeology. He held posts as Duesenberg Professor of Christianity and the Arts at Valparaiso University (~1990–2008) and as professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1999–2010).

David N. Lorenzen is a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He studied at SOAS and the Australian National University (~1965–1968) under Arthur Llewellyn Basham and J. G. de Casparis, later joining El Colegio de México (~1970).

David Ownby is an academic in sinology, religious studies, and history and archaeology. He earned his Ph.D. at Harvard University (~1982–1989), taught at Southern Methodist University (~1990–1993), and became professor of history at Université de Montréal in 1994.

David P. Jackson specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Washington under David Seyfort Ruegg, among others, and with traditional teachers including Dezhung Rinpoche. He served as a C-3 professor at the University of Hamburg (1992–2007).

David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1993 under doctoral supervisor Geshe Lhundub Sopa, also studying under traditional teachers Geshe Lobsang Tenzin and Geshe Thubten Tandhar.

David Phillip Stanley specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Virginia (~2001–2009) under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. He later served as associate professor at Naropa University (~2009) and co-director of Nitartha Institute.

David Pingree was an Indology and history and archaeology scholar. He studied at Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer. He held posts at Harvard, the University of Chicago (1963–1971), and Brown University as professor (1971–2007).

David R. Loy works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Carleton College, the University of Hawaii, and the National University of Singapore (Ph.D.), where he also taught (~1978–1984), later serving as professor at Xavier University (~2006–2009).

David Ralph Quinter specializes in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He studied at the University of Colorado Boulder and earned his Ph.D. at Stanford University (~2000–2006) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later becoming associate professor at the University of Alberta (~2008).

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Educated at Gonville and Caius College, he served as Lecturer in Tibetan at Cambridge (~1948–1955) and held posts at Jesus College, Michigan (1968–1975), and Harvard (1975–1982).
David Ruddell was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He studied at Laval University and served as Secretary at Fort William College.
David Schaberg is a sinologist who studied at Stanford University (~1982–1986) and Harvard University (~1989–1996). He took up a post at the University of California, Los Angeles in ~1996.

David Seyfort Ruegg was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Paris under Jean Filliozat, Louis Renou, and Rolf Alfred Stein, holding professorial posts at Leiden, Washington, Hamburg, and SOAS University of London.

David Shulman is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1968–1972) and the University of London (~1972–1976). He held posts at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem beginning in 1976 and at the University of Chicago.

David Tracy is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Saint Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University. He held academic posts at the Catholic University of America (~1967–1969) and the University of Chicago (~1969–2006).

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He pursued doctoral work at Yale University (~1968–1976) and served as professor at the University of Hawaii (~1972–2000) and at Soka University of America (~2000–2004).

David W. Tien is a sinology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Toronto, McGill University, and the University of Michigan (~2002–2009, Ph.D.), where his supervisors were James Robson and Philip J. Ivanhoe.

David Webster is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the University of Bristol and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Sunderland (~1999–2003) under doctoral supervisor Peter Harvey.

Dawa Norbu was a Tibetology and history scholar. He studied at the University of Delhi (~1970–1974) and the University of California, Berkeley (~1976–1977), and held posts at San Francisco State University and Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1983–2004).

Daya Ram Sahni was an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at Oriental College, Lahore (~1898–1903). He served as Deputy for Exploration at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931–1935) and Director of Archæology and Historical Research in Jaipur State (1935).
